overflow_result_assumption.decision_summary: Human reviewer approved the project-level formalization assumption that, for base scalar PTX add.u32, the formalized destination value is the mathematical sum reduced modulo 2^32, equivalently the low 32 bits of the sum. The record explicitly states this assumption is NOT an NVIDIA SOURCE FACT and must never be presented as explicitly specified by NVIDIA; semantic interpretation, Lean definitions, executable semantics, bit-width theorems, examples, and final traceability must reference this human-approved assumption.

syntax.guarded_form: @p add.u32 d, a, b;  (equivalently @!p add.u32 d, a, b;)
syntax_notes: .u32 is listed in .type2, the operand set of the add{.sat}.type2 syntax line; the base add.u32 form is the .sat-absent instantiation of that line.
The optional guard predicate is omitted from instruction-description syntax (section 9.7) but may prefix any PTX instruction as @{!}p (section 9.3).

Only the base scalar form add.u32 is the semantic unit of this interpretation. add.sat.u32 and the packed forms (add.u16x2, add.s16x2, add.u8x4, add.s8x4 and their sat forms) are recorded only as out-of-scope context, never as semantic units.

operands.order: d, a, b (destination first, then two sources)

roles.d: destination operand. For instructions that create a result value, d is the destination operand; add performs addition and writes the resulting value into a destination register. The destination is a register variable of the instruction type in the .reg state space, or, per the general section 9.2 bit-bucket rule, the underscore bit bucket '_'.
roles.a: source operand. A register variable of compatible type or a constant immediate.
roles.b: source operand. A register variable of compatible type or a constant immediate.

operand_forms_supported_by_evidence: source constant immediate (PTX-9.3-ADD-012; PTX-9.3-ADD-025 shows immediate 4)
destination bit bucket '_' per the general section 9.2 rule (PTX-9.3-ADD-015); add-specific demonstration absent, see AMB-1
operand_form_evidence_notes: PTX-9.3-ADD-004: 'writes the resulting value into a destination register' establishes a register destination.
PTX-9.3-ADD-012: integer arithmetic instructions (family including add) operate on the integer types in register and constant immediate forms.
PTX-9.3-ADD-025: official example add.u32 %r, %r, 4 with .reg .u32 declarations, a constant immediate source, and the destination aliasing source a.
PTX-9.3-ADD-026: official example add.u32 %res, %ptr, %inc with all three operands .reg .u32 registers.

types.operand_typing_rule: For the scalar instruction type .u32, operands d, a and b have the same type as the instruction type. The .b32 exception is stated by the source only for the enumerated packed types .u16x2, .s16x2, .u8x4, .s8x4.
types.compatibility_rules: Operand types and sizes are checked against instruction types for compatibility. Two fundamental types are compatible if they have the same basic type and are the same size; signed and unsigned integer types are compatible if they have the same size; the bit-size type is compatible with any fundamental type of the same size.

static_preconditions.description: Operands d, a, b have the same type as the instruction type .u32, or a type compatible with .u32 under the section 5.2.1 compatibility rules (same basic type and same size; or signed/unsigned same size; or bit-size of same size).
The destination operand d denotes a register variable (of the instruction type in the .reg state space) or, per the general section 9.2 rule, the bit bucket '_'.
Source operands a and b are register variables of compatible type or constant immediates (integer arithmetic instructions operate in register and constant immediate forms).
If a guard is present, it is a predicate register variable of type .pred in the register state space, optionally negated.
Version gating: base add (and therefore base add.u32) is introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.
Target gating: base add is supported on all target architectures.

dynamic_preconditions.description: No dynamic precondition is stated in the evidence for add.u32 (for example, no requirement on the values held by source operands, and no carry-flag or status-register requirement). None is asserted. The arithmetic rule applies to all .u32 source operand values under the human-approved result rule (PTX-ADD-SEM2-015).

state_reads.description: When a is a register, its current (pre-instruction) value is read from the value-register file; when a is a constant immediate, the immediate value is used.
When b is a register, its current (pre-instruction) value is read from the value-register file; when b is a constant immediate, the immediate value is used.

state_reads.component: guard predicate register p (when a guard is present)
state_reads.description: The value of the predicate register referenced by the guard is read to evaluate the complete guard expression.

state_writes.component: destination register d (on execution with a real destination register)
state_writes.description: When the complete guard expression evaluates true and d is a register, the destination register d is updated with the resulting value (a + b) mod 2^32 under the human-approved assumption. Only the destination update required by the bounded semantics is proposed: no other value register, predicate register, carry flag, or status/condition-code component is written by base add.u32.

When the destination is the bit bucket '_', the general section 9.2 rule indicates the destination register is replaced by the bit bucket; the represented consequence is that no value register is written (the result is discarded). This is a derived interpretation supported only to the strength of the general rule; add-specific demonstration is absent (AMB-1).

state_writes.component: state when the complete guard expression evaluates false
state_writes.description: When the complete guard expression evaluates false, the thread does nothing: the instruction is not executed and no machine-state component changes (no destination update, no source modification, no predicate-register modification). This is derived from the explicit predication clause in section 9.7.13.2 applied to add.u32; it is source-supported, not a human assumption.

guard_semantics.guard_expression_representation: An optional guard prefix @{!}p appears after an @ symbol to the left of the opcode, where p is a predicate register variable of type .pred. The guard may be negated with '!'. No guard is present in the syntax-description form (the optional guard predicate is omitted from the syntax), but all PTX instructions may be predicated.

guard_expression_evaluation.no_guard: The complete guard expression is true; the instruction is executed unconditionally.
guard_expression_evaluation.at_p: @p: the complete guard expression is the value of predicate register p; execution occurs when p is true.
guard_expression_evaluation.at_bang_p: @!p: the complete guard expression is the logical negation of the value of predicate register p; execution occurs when p is false. The official example '@!p bra L1; // if False, branch over' shows the negated guard executing when the underlying predicate is false.
guard_expression_evaluation.execution_condition: Execution occurs if and only if the complete guard expression evaluates true. The underlying predicate value is not confused with the evaluated guard expression: for @!p, the guard expression is true exactly when the predicate value is false.

guard_semantics.guard_false_consequence: The predication construct section 9.7.13.2 explicitly states: 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' with Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PDF page 400; HTML anchor control-flow-instructions-at, lines 21826-21841). For add.u32, a false complete guard expression therefore means the thread does nothing: the guarded instruction is not executed and no machine-state component changes. This resolves BLOCK-2 by official specification evidence; it is not treated as a human assumption.
guard_semantics.predication_exception: st.param and ld.param instructions used for argument passing cannot be predicated; this exception does not mention add and therefore does not restrict add.u32 predication.

behavior.arithmetic_semantic_rule: For the scalar instruction types, including .u32, the add Semantics block gives the rule 'd = a + b;' (the final else branch; the first two branches handle only the packed .u16x2/.s16x2 and .u8x4/.s8x4 types). The prose meaning statements are 'Add two values.' and 'Performs addition and writes the resulting value into a destination register.'
behavior.semantics_notation_note: Section 9.6 states that semantics are 'described using C, until C is not expressive enough' (PDF page 138; PTX-9.3-ADD-SUP2-002). This is a notation/framing statement about how the Semantics blocks are written; it does not import ISO C arithmetic rules into PTX, and no C overflow semantics are used in this interpretation.
behavior.result_rule: When the complete guard expression evaluates true and the destination is a register, the value written to the destination register d is the mathematical sum of the source values reduced modulo 2^32, equivalently the low 32 bits of the mathematical sum: d := (a + b) mod 2^32. This rule is the human-approved formalization assumption (PTX-ADD-SEM2-015); it is NOT an NVIDIA source fact and is never attributed to NVIDIA as explicitly specified.
behavior.result_rule_classification: HUMAN_APPROVED_ASSUMPTION (PTX-ADD-SEM2-015); the fully determined destination-update consequence is DERIVED_INTERPRETATION (PTX-ADD-SEM2-016) explicitly depending on that assumption.
behavior.guard_true_behavior: When the complete guard expression evaluates true (including the no-guard case), the instruction executes: the pre-instruction values of source operands a and b are read (register values or constant immediates), the result (a + b) mod 2^32 is computed under the human-approved assumption, and the destination register d is updated with that result; if d is the bit bucket '_', no register is written.
behavior.guard_false_behavior: When the complete guard expression evaluates false, the thread does nothing: the instruction is not executed and the machine state is unchanged (source-supported via section 9.7.13.2; see PTX-ADD-SEM2-022, PTX-ADD-SEM2-024, PTX-ADD-SEM2-031).
behavior.aliasing_read_before_write: The destination register may also appear as a source operand (official example add.u32 %r, %r, 4 has d == a). The result is computed from the source values read before the destination update, so a destination that aliases a source does not corrupt the source value used.
behavior.determinism_note: Determinism is not explicitly stated in the source (GAP-3); it is derived in this interpretation from the fully-specified rules and is stated as proof obligation PRF-1 (see determinism section and PTX-ADD-SEM2-042).

exceptional_behavior.statement: No explicit error, trap, or exceptional-behavior clause for add (or add.u32) was found in the evidence (bundle coverage area 17 status NOT_FOUND; GAP-4). This absence is not asserted as a positive source fact that no exceptional behavior exists; no error, trap, or exceptional behavior is invented. Whether the absence means no such behaviors exist is recorded as open question PTX-ADD-SEM2-044.

undefined_behavior.statement: No explicit undefined-behavior clause for add (or add.u32) was found in the evidence (GAP-4). No undefined-behavior claim is made; no undefined behavior is invented.

implementation_defined_behavior.statement: No explicit implementation-defined-behavior clause for add (or add.u32) was found in the evidence. No implementation-defined-behavior claim is made; no implementation-defined behavior is invented.

determinism.statement: The execution relation for add.u32 is deterministic: for any well-formed state and well-typed add.u32 instruction, the fully-specified rules determine at most one resulting state. The guard evaluation is a deterministic function of the predicate register value; the arithmetic result is a deterministic function of the source values under the human-approved modulo rule; and the only state write on execution is the destination update. Determinism is NOT explicitly stated in the source (bundle gap GAP-3); it is a derived interpretation that depends on the human-approved assumption (PTX-ADD-SEM2-015) and the source-supported guard rule (PTX-ADD-SEM2-024), and it is stated as proof obligation PRF-1.

version_restrictions.base_add_u32_introduced_in: PTX ISA version 1.0 (derived: base add introduced in 1.0 and add.u32 is a base, non-saturating form of add; add.sat.u32 is separately introduced in 9.2 and is out of scope).

target_restrictions.note: The sm_90 note (add.u16x2/add.s16x2) and the family-specific sm_120f note (add.sat.u32 and other sat/packed forms) concern only future saturating/packed forms outside the bounded base unit; the formal meaning of 'same family' is not defined in the evidence (PTX-ADD-SEM2-056).

semantic_claims.statement: The construct identity is the add instruction family: PTX ISA 9.3 section 9.7.1.1 'Integer Arithmetic Instructions: add', HTML anchor integer-arithmetic-instructions-add (HTML lines 8757-8760).
Section 9.1 states that each PTX instruction is described by its name, format, semantics, and examples; this frames the add Syntax/Semantics/Examples blocks as normative source content.

The exact add syntax variants are 'add.type1 d, a, b;' and 'add{.sat}.type2 d, a, b;' with .type1 = { .u16, .u64, .s16, .s64 } and .type2 = { .u32, .u16x2, .u8x4, .s32, .s16x2, .s8x4 }; .u32 is listed in .type2; the base add.u32 form is the .sat-absent instantiation of the second syntax line.

Operand order and role conventions: section 9.2 states 'For instructions that create a result value, the d operand is the destination operand, while a, b, and c are source operands' and that an optional guard predicate appears after an @ symbol to the left of the opcode; the d, a, b form matches add.u32.
The add meaning statement is 'Add two values.'
The add execution description is 'Performs addition and writes the resulting value into a destination register.'

d is the destination operand, and a and b are source operands, for base add.u32. When executing with a real destination register, the only state write proposed by the bounded semantics is the destination update; no other value register, predicate register, carry flag, or status/condition-code component is proposed to be written because the source states no such write for base add.
Operand typing: 'Operands d, a and b have the same type as the instruction type.' The source states the .b32 exception only for the enumerated packed instruction types .u16x2, .s16x2, .u8x4, .s8x4.

.u32 is an unsigned integer fundamental type specifier; a fundamental type specifies both a basic type and a size; register variables are always of a fundamental type and instructions operate on these types; the same type-size specifiers are used for variable definitions and instruction typing.

Registers (.reg state space) are fast storage locations; aside from 1-bit predicate registers, scalar registers have a width of 8-, 16-, 32-, 64-, or 128-bits (32-bit width is therefore possible for .u32 registers); registers are not fully addressable.

Type compatibility: operand types and sizes are checked against instruction types for compatibility; two fundamental types are compatible if they have the same basic type and are the same size; signed and unsigned integer types are compatible if they have the same size; the bit-size type is compatible with any fundamental type having the same size.

For this unit, add.u32 denotes the scalar, non-saturating, unsigned 32-bit form of add: it is the .u32 entry of the base syntax without the .sat modifier; because .u32 is not among the packed types enumerated in the first two semantics branches, the applicable semantics branch is the final else clause 'd = a + b;'; and because the .b32 exception is enumerated only for packed types, operands d, a, b all have type .u32 (unsigned integer, size 32).

The add Semantics block (lines 8785-8811) contains, verbatim, three branches: a packed half-word branch (.u16x2/.s16x2), a packed quarter-word branch (.u8x4/.s8x4), and a final else branch whose statement is 'd = a + b;'.

Section 9.6 (PDF page 138) states: 'The goal of the semantic description of an instruction is to describe the results in all cases in as simple language as possible. The semantics are described using C, until C is not expressive enough.' This is a notation statement about how Semantics blocks are written; the PTX text contains no normative import of ISO C arithmetic rules, and this interpretation does not use C overflow semantics for add.u32.

For base scalar PTX add.u32, the formalized destination value is the mathematical sum of the two source values reduced modulo 2^32, equivalently the low 32 bits of the mathematical sum: d := (a + b) mod 2^32. This is the human-approved project-level formalization assumption; it is NOT an NVIDIA source fact and is never presented as explicitly specified by NVIDIA. The assumption is approved because no official PTX ISA 9.3 normative rule was found in either the HTML or the PDF determining the exact .u32 result when the mathematical sum exceeds the unsigned 32-bit range (BLOCK-1 NOT_FOUND; the 'd = a + b;' pseudocode is uninterpreted, the 9.6 'described using C' statement does not import C overflow rules, and the only truncation statements found are instruction-specific to ld/st/cvt and redux.sync).

human_assumption_reference.note: See human_assumption_references.overflow_result_assumption for the full traceability note; the decision record's own SHA-256 is not published in the repository and no value is fabricated.

semantic_claims.statement: Given the human-approved result rule, the destination update on execution is fully determined for all .u32 source operand pairs: when the complete guard expression evaluates true and d is a register, d is updated with (a + b) mod 2^32.
All PTX instructions may be predicated; in the instruction descriptions the optional guard predicate is omitted from the syntax.

All instructions have an optional guard predicate which controls conditional execution of the instruction; the syntax is to prefix an instruction with @{!}p, where p is a predicate variable, optionally negated; instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally.
The official add Examples block includes the predicated form '@p add.u32 x,y,z;', so guarded add.u32 is in scope.

Official guard examples: '@p add.s32 j, j, 1; // if i < n, add 1 to j' and '@!p bra L1; // if False, branch over'; the @p example uses an add instruction and the @!p example shows the negated guard executing when the underlying predicate is false.
Predicate registers are virtual and have .pred as the type specifier and may be declared as '.reg .pred p, q, r;'.

The predication construct section 9.7.13.2 (Control Flow Instructions: @) explicitly states: 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' with Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction'. The clause exists in both the official PDF (page 400) and the official HTML (anchor control-flow-instructions-at, lines 21826-21841).

Complete guard-expression evaluation model: no guard -> the complete guard expression is true (unconditional execution); @p -> the complete guard expression is the value of predicate register p; @!p -> the complete guard expression is the logical negation of the value of predicate register p. The instruction executes if and only if the complete guard expression evaluates true. The underlying predicate value is not confused with the evaluated guard expression.

When the complete guard expression evaluates false for add.u32, the thread does nothing: the instruction is not executed and no machine-state component changes (the destination register d is not updated, source operands are not modified, the guard predicate register is not modified, and no other value-register or predicate-register component changes). This is derived from the explicit predication clause (section 9.7.13.2; PDF page 400; HTML lines 21826-21841) applied to add.u32 via universal predication ('All PTX instructions may be predicated') and the official guarded add example '@p add.u32 x,y,z;'. BLOCK-2 is resolved by official specification evidence, not by a human assumption.

State read: the instruction reads source operand a. When a is a register, its current (pre-instruction) value is read from the value-register file; when a is a constant immediate, the immediate value is used.

State read: the instruction reads source operand b. When b is a register, its current (pre-instruction) value is read from the value-register file; when b is a constant immediate, the immediate value is used.
State read: when a guard is present, the value of the predicate register referenced by the guard is read to evaluate the complete guard expression.

State write: when the instruction executes, the destination register d is updated with the resulting value. The source states no other register write for base add.u32 (no carry flag, status register, or condition-code component).

State write detail: when executing with a real destination register, only the destination update required by the bounded semantics is proposed, and the update value is (a + b) mod 2^32 under the human-approved assumption (PTX-ADD-SEM2-015). No other state write is proposed.

Bit-bucket destination: per the general section 9.2 rule, an underscore '_' may be used in place of a destination register. The represented consequence for add.u32 is that when d is '_', execution performs no register write (the result is discarded). This consequence is supported only to the strength of the general rule; the add section does not demonstrate the bit-bucket form (AMB-1).
State write when the complete guard expression evaluates false: no state write occurs; the thread does nothing and the machine state is unchanged (source-supported via section 9.7.13.2).
Static precondition: operands d, a, b have the same type as the instruction type .u32, or a type compatible with .u32 under the section 5.2.1 compatibility rules.
Static precondition: the destination operand d denotes a register variable of the instruction type in the .reg state space or, per the general section 9.2 rule, the bit bucket '_'.

Static precondition: source operands a and b are register variables of compatible type or constant immediates (integer arithmetic instructions operate in register and constant immediate forms; official examples demonstrate both).
Static precondition: if a guard is present, it is a predicate register variable of type .pred in the register state space, optionally negated.

Version gating: because .u32 without .sat is one of the base add forms in the Syntax block and the PTX ISA Notes assign version 1.0 to base add while assigning version 9.2 only to add.sat.u32 and other sat/packed forms, the base add.u32 form is introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.
Target gating: the Target ISA Notes state that base add is supported on all target architectures.
No dynamic precondition is stated in the evidence for add.u32 (for example, no requirement on the values held by source operands, and no carry-flag or status-register requirement). None is asserted.

PTX ISA Notes: 'Introduced in PTX ISA version 1.0.' for base add; add.u16x2 and add.s16x2 introduced in version 8.0; add{.sat}.u8x4, add{.sat}.s8x4, add.sat.u16x2, add.sat.s16x2 and add.sat.u32 introduced in version 9.2.

Target ISA Notes: 'Supported on all target architectures.' for base add; the sm_90 note (add.u16x2/add.s16x2) and the family-specific sm_120f note (add.sat.u32 and other sat/packed forms) concern forms outside the bounded base unit.

The .sat modifier 'limits result to MININT..MAXINT (no overflow) for the size and signedness of the operation' and applies to .u32 among other types; this concerns the separate saturating form add.sat.u32 and is not part of the base add.u32 unit. Base add applicability is therefore separated from add.sat.u32 restrictions.

Determinism: the fully-specified rules (source-supported guard rule and human-approved arithmetic rule) determine at most one resulting state for each well-formed state and well-typed add.u32 instruction. Determinism is NOT explicitly stated in the source (GAP-3); this is a derived interpretation depending on the human-approved assumption and is stated as proof obligation PRF-1.

Aliasing/read-before-write: the destination register may also appear as a source operand (official example 'add.u32 %r, %r, 4;' has d == a). The result is computed from the source values read before the destination update, so a destination that aliases a source does not corrupt the source value used.

No explicit error, trap, or exceptional-behavior clause for add (or add.u32) was found in the evidence (bundle coverage area 17 NOT_FOUND; GAP-4). The absence is not asserted as a positive source fact; no error or trap behavior is invented.
No explicit undefined-behavior clause for add (or add.u32) was found in the evidence (GAP-4). No undefined-behavior claim is made.
No explicit implementation-defined-behavior clause for add (or add.u32) was found in the evidence. No implementation-defined-behavior claim is made.
For some instructions the destination operand is optional; a bit bucket operand denoted with an underscore (_) may be used in place of a destination register (general section 9.2 rule).

Instruction representation design (architecture D-1, D-2, D-16): an add.u32 instruction is represented as an optional guard (@{!}p), mnemonic add, type specifier .u32, empty modifier set for the base form, destination operand, and source operands a, b in that order.

Minimal machine state design (architecture D-5, D-14): the state for base add.u32 is the pair (value-register file, predicate-register file); no memory, shared, special-register, or concurrency state is required by the add.u32 syntax and description.

Execution-result representation design (architecture D-8): an instruction-local outcome has at least two cases, executed (with updated destination) and guard-false (thread does nothing; no state change); no error constructor is proposed because no explicit exceptional behavior for base add is evidenced.

Version and target representation design (architecture D-9, D-22, D-23): base add.u32 is represented with an introduced-in bound of PTX ISA 1.0 and a target requirement of all target architectures; family-specific target machinery is explicitly out of scope for the base unit.

Execution-semantics representation design (architecture D-25): the future execution semantics for add.u32 is designed to be represented as an execution relation between (state, instruction) and state, not merely as a function, so that determinism and frame/locality obligations are non-vacuous.

The allowed range and encoding of constant immediate source operands for add are not stated in the evidence; only the rule that integer arithmetic instructions operate in register and constant immediate forms and the example immediate 4 were found (bundle gap GAP-5).

Add-specific bit-bucket destination behavior is not explicitly stated; the general section 9.2 rule supports the '_' destination form, but the add section does not demonstrate it (bundle gap GAP-6; AMB-1).

Whether the absence of an explicit error, trap, or undefined-behavior clause (bundle gap GAP-4) means base add has no such behaviors, or whether such behaviors exist but are not stated in the read sections, is unresolved.
The formal meaning of 'sm_120f or higher in the same family' is not defined in the evidence; this concerns only future saturating/packed forms outside the bounded base unit (bundle gap GAP-8).

PDF page numbers for the primary-bundle fragments are null because the PDF was not read in the primary curation pass (bundle gap GAP-7); the supplementary pass read the PDF and recorded page numbers only for supplementary fragments. No PDF page numbers were fabricated.

The SHA-256 of the human assumption decision record (reviews/ptx-add-u32/assumptions/ptx-add-u32-overflow-assumption-v1.json) is not published in the repository and was not computable in this semantic stage. The canonical decision path is cited for every HUMAN_APPROVED_ASSUMPTION claim; a future verification pass should compute and record the decision record's own SHA-256.

resolved_blockers.previous_status: NOT_FOUND after official HTML and PDF search (add-u32-blockers-supplement-v2.json)
resolved_blockers.resolution_summary: The exact base scalar add.u32 result when the mathematical sum exceeds the unsigned 32-bit range is not determined by any official PTX ISA 9.3 normative text (BLOCK-1 NOT_FOUND; supplement fragments SUP2-001 through SUP2-004 document the searched context). The human reviewer approved the project-level formalization assumption: the formalized destination value is the mathematical sum reduced modulo 2^32, equivalently the low 32 bits.
resolved_blockers.classification_rule: No claim depending on the modulo-2^32 rule is classified SOURCE_FACT; modulo behavior is never attributed to NVIDIA as explicitly specified. Claims depending on it are classified HUMAN_APPROVED_ASSUMPTION or DERIVED_INTERPRETATION with an explicit dependency on that assumption.

resolved_blockers.previous_status: PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED per the v1 critic; bundle gap GAP-2
resolved_blockers.resolution_summary: Section 9.7.13.2 (Control Flow Instructions: @) explicitly states 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' with Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PDF page 400; HTML anchor control-flow-instructions-at, lines 21826-21841). Since all PTX instructions may be predicated and the add Examples include '@p add.u32 x,y,z;', the false-guard machine-state effect for add.u32 is that the thread does nothing: the instruction is not executed and no state component changes.
resolved_blockers.not_treated_as: BLOCK-2 is not treated as a human assumption; the official specification evidence is sufficient.

assumptions.summary: For base scalar PTX add.u32, the formalized destination value is (a + b) mod 2^32, equivalently the low 32 bits of the mathematical sum. Approved by the human reviewer in reviews/ptx-add-u32/assumptions/ptx-add-u32-overflow-assumption-v1.json. NOT an NVIDIA source fact; never attributed to NVIDIA as explicitly specified.
assumptions.note: This is the only HUMAN_APPROVED_ASSUMPTION in this interpretation. The v1 assumptions SEM-038 (guard-false 'no state update' pending approval) and SEM-040 (PDF not read) are superseded in v2: BLOCK-2 is resolved by official evidence and the PDF was read in the supplementary pass. The v1 assumption SEM-039 (no error constructor) is re-expressed as design dependency PTX-ADD-SEM2-050 plus open questions PTX-ADD-SEM2-044/PTX-ADD-SEM2-055.

ambiguities.description: The general section 9.2 bit-bucket rule says '_' may be used in place of a destination register 'for some instructions'; whether add.u32 is one of those instructions is not demonstrated in the add section. The architecture treats the bit bucket as a supported destination form by design (D-18), grounded only in the general rule; the represented no-write consequence is supported only to that strength.
ambiguities.impact: Non-blocking for the base register-destination semantics; affects the exact set of well-formed destination forms and the strength of PRF-3.

ambiguities.description: The '+' operator in the semantics block 'd = a + b;' is not defined by the source with respect to overflow: no statement whether the addition is modular (wrapping) on the 32-bit type, truncated, unspecified, or otherwise when the mathematical sum exceeds 2^32-1.
ambiguities.impact: Resolved for formalization by the human-approved assumption PTX-ADD-SEM2-015; the resulting 32-bit value is now determined for all operand values.

ambiguities.description: The exact machine-state consequence of a false guard predicate was not stated in the primary evidence; 'controls conditional execution' admitted the natural reading 'instruction does not execute and the state is unchanged'.
ambiguities.impact: Resolved by official specification evidence (section 9.7.13.2: threads with a False guard predicate do nothing); not treated as a human assumption.

ambiguities.description: The allowed range and encoding of constant immediate source operands for add are not stated; the only evidence is the family rule and an example with immediate 4.
ambiguities.impact: Non-blocking for the arithmetic result of a given legal immediate; affects static well-formedness of programs.

ambiguities.description: Whether the absence of an explicit error/undefined-behavior clause for add means such behaviors do not exist, or exist but are unstated in the read sections, is unresolved.
ambiguities.impact: Non-blocking as an absence record; would become blocking if positive error behavior is later evidenced.

ambiguities.description: Whether the destination register d may alias a source operand a or b, and how the result is computed in that case.
ambiguities.impact: Resolved by derivation: d may alias a source (official example 'add.u32 %r, %r, 4;' has d == a), and the result is computed from the pre-instruction source values (read-before-write); see PTX-ADD-SEM2-043.

future_theorem_obligation_topics.description: Determinism of the execution relation for add.u32: at most one resulting state for any well-formed state and well-typed instruction. No longer blocked; supported by the fully-specified rules (derived interpretation PTX-ADD-SEM2-042, which depends on PTX-ADD-SEM2-015 and PTX-ADD-SEM2-024).

Destination-only update / frame: when add.u32 executes with a register destination, only the destination register may change; every other value register and predicate register is unchanged. No longer blocked.

Bit-bucket discard: when the destination is '_', execution changes no value register. Depends on the general-rule-supported bit-bucket interpretation (AMB-1; PTX-ADD-SEM2-030); add-specific demonstration remains an open question (PTX-ADD-SEM2-054), which is non-blocking for the base register-destination semantics.

Guard-false frame: when the complete guard expression evaluates false, the entire state is unchanged. No longer blocked; supported by official specification evidence (section 9.7.13.2; PTX-ADD-SEM2-024, PTX-ADD-SEM2-031). The theorem must not classify this behavior as SOURCE_FACT for add.u32; it is a DERIVED_INTERPRETATION from the explicit predication clause.

Guard-behavior: the instruction executes if and only if the complete guard expression evaluates true, covering no-guard, @p, and @!p cases uniformly. No longer blocked; PTX-ADD-SEM2-023/PTX-ADD-SEM2-024.

Result-domain membership: when add.u32 executes, the value written to the destination lies in the 32-bit unsigned value domain. No longer blocked; domain membership is established (PTX-ADD-SEM2-031/v1 SEM-031 analog) and the exact value is fixed by PTX-ADD-SEM2-016.

Arithmetic result correctness: the value written to the destination equals the mathematical sum reduced modulo 2^32. No longer blocked; the theorem must carry traceability to the HUMAN_APPROVED_ASSUMPTION PTX-ADD-SEM2-015 and must never classify the modulo-2^32 rule as SOURCE_FACT or attribute it to NVIDIA as explicitly specified.

critic_review_reference.note: The v1 critic found BLOCK-1 UNSUPPORTED (recommended REQUIRE_MORE_OFFICIAL_SOURCE_SEARCH, completed by supplement v2) and BLOCK-2 PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED (recommended HUMAN_APPROVED_FORMALIZATION_ASSUMPTION). After supplement v2, BLOCK-2 is resolved by explicit official evidence, and BLOCK-1 by the human-approved assumption; this v2 revision supersedes the v1 interpretation accordingly.

traceability_summary.evidence_interface_note: No raw PTX HTML or PDF was read in this semantic stage; all semantic claims reference source-bundle and supplement fragment IDs only.
traceability_summary.classification_note: Modulo-2^32 behavior is never classified as SOURCE_FACT and is never attributed to NVIDIA as explicitly specified; all claims depending on it are classified HUMAN_APPROVED_ASSUMPTION or DERIVED_INTERPRETATION with an explicit dependency on PTX-ADD-SEM2-015. BLOCK-2 guard-false behavior is source-supported via the explicit section 9.7.13.2 predication clause and is not treated as a human assumption.
